Jordan — looping back with suggested bite-sized language that procurement/product can use directly. I started from your asks and kept things short. Feel free to inline edits.

Proposed glossary bullets (sales-facing, max 2 lines each):
- What is a subprocessor? A subprocessor is a third-party vendor Redwood uses to run or maintain the service (e.g., GPUs, monitoring). Some subprocessors may handle encrypted customer content only for short-lived processing; others support infrastructure and don't access customer content.
- Will customer content leave my region? We offer region-selectable storage for customer content; when you choose a residency region, primary storage and backups remain in that region. For customers on hosted API without an explicit residency contract, data may be processed or routed across regions to serve traffic; we rely on SCCs and additional technical safeguards for cross-border transfers.
- What about logs and telemetry? Logs that include operational metadata (latency, error traces) are retained to troubleshoot and improve service; logs containing customer content are minimized and subject to retention controls.

Procurement-ready sentence for vendor registry (one line):
- Redwood commits to Standard Contractual Clauses (or an equivalent transfer mechanism) for transfers outside the EU and provides region-selectable storage for customers who require data residency.

Technical/nuance note for legal: to be 100% precise we need to confirm which subprocessors have KV-cache access — I flagged that with Infra and attached the latest spreadsheet.

Draft doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=example-doc-privacy-glossary (internal edit access)

Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions Enablement, Redwood Inference
